item.title: Miscreants set fire to ex-minister Mozammel Haque’s house in Gazipur
item.description:
Miscreants have set fire to the house of former liberation war affairs minister and activities-banned Gazipur district Awami League President AKM Mozammel Haque in Gazipur.
Two Fire Service units rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control.
The incident took place around 8:30pm on Tuesday at the house in the Dakshin Chayabithi (Jor Pukurpar) area of Gazipur city.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Gazipur Sadar Police Station Aminul Islam said the house targeted in the arson attack was Mozammel Haque’s old tin-shed residence.
He said an eight-storey building owned by the former minister stands nearby and remained untouched. The tin-shed house had been rented out.
According to the OC, a group of miscreants forced the tenants out of their rooms before setting the house on fire around 8:30pm. The flames quickly spread throughout the structure.
Two Fire Service units reached the scene and brought the fire under control around 9:15pm after nearly half an hour of efforts.
However, Gazipur Fire Service Deputy Assistant Director Saidul Alam Chowdhury said they had yet to confirm the ownership of the tin-shed house in the Jor Pukurpar area.
"Some people say it belongs to the former minister, while others claim it belongs to someone else," he said.
He added that two Fire Service units responded to the incident and brought the fire under control.

item.title: Hasnat calls India ‘largest house of cross-border terrorists’
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Senior Joint Convener and lawmaker Hasnat Abdullah on Tuesday described India as the “largest house of cross-border terrorists”, accusing it of providing shelter and support to leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League, who were attempting to create instability in Bangladesh.
“India is the largest house of cross-border terrorists. Those who threaten Bangladesh's sovereignty and have killed people in this country are being provided shelter there,” he said.
Hasnat also urged the government to question India over its alleged role and seek a clear explanation about its position, saying the activities posed a direct challenge to the country's sovereignty.
He alleged that people involved in activities against Bangladesh were operating from Indian territory, carrying out violence in the country and returning to India, while New Delhi remained silent.
The NCP leader was addressing a discussion titled “One Year of the Verdict: Sheikh Hasina's Trial, Extradition and State Accountability”, arranged by the party’s July Mass Uprising Cell to mark the first anniversary of the death sentence against Sheikh Hasina for crimes against humanity during the July 2024 mass uprising.
He also accused India of applying double standards on cross-border security issues.
To explain his position, Hasnat presented a hypothetical example of Bangladesh providing shelter to an ULFA leader and allowing the individual to organise attacks and violent activities in India's Assam from Dhaka.
He questioned whether India would tolerate such activities if they were directed against its own territory, arguing that New Delhi was unwilling to accept a situation that it was allegedly allowing in Bangladesh's case.
The NCP leader further alleged that India had been providing training and shelter to people involved in cross-border violence over the past two and a half years.
He said Bangladesh respected international protocols and India's sovereignty but could not remain silent over activities that threatened its own sovereignty.
Hasnat called on the government to raise the issue with India and demand clarification over how it had allegedly become a “safe haven” for people involved in terrorism against Bangladesh.

item.title: Law minister: Pallabi child murder trial completed, Hadi case to follow
item.description:
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has said the trial of Sharif Osman Hadi's murder will be ensured, announcing that appeals in the Major Sinha, Biswajit and Abrar Fahad murder cases will begin hearing at the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court from next week.
He also said the trial in the rape and murder case of eight-year-old Pallabi girl had concluded, with the accused sentenced to death.
The minister made the remarks in a statement under Rule 300 during the seventh day of the fourth session of the 13th parliament on Tuesday.
Recalling the Pallabi girl case, Asaduzzaman said the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl in May had deeply shaken the nation.
He said the child was raped and murdered by her neighbour, Sohel Rana, on May 19. Police arrested Rana and his wife on the same day. A case was filed the following day, and the charge sheet was submitted to the court on May 24. After completing the legal proceedings, the court delivered its verdict on June 17, sentencing both accused to death.
The law minister said the appeal in the case was also disposed of in the shortest time in the country's judicial history for a death penalty case.
He acknowledged the roles of the prime minister, the home minister, the chief justice and other concerned authorities in ensuring a speedy trial. He also thanked the Attorney General's Office and all those involved in the process.
Asaduzzaman said the girl's father had initially been reluctant to file a case, fearing that his family would not get justice. The prime minister, home minister and law minister later visited the victim's home and assured the family of justice and support. "The government has worked to fulfil that promise," he said.
The minister said the government had pledged to uphold justice despite all obstacles since taking office.
Ensuring justice for those who had disappeared, lost their lives, been subjected to enforced disappearance or political persecution, or fallen victim to crimes against humanity over the past 16–17 years was the state's responsibility, he said.
He added that the government would take initiatives to begin trials of crimes against humanity in districts across the country. On Hadi's murder, Asaduzzaman said the government was giving the investigation and trial the highest priority and taking all necessary measures on behalf of the state.
He also announced that appeals in the Major Sinha, Biswajit and Abrar Fahad murder cases would be heard by the Appellate Division in phases from next week, describing the move as part of the government's commitment to ensuring justice.
Seeking cooperation from opposition lawmakers, the law minister said the government would continue its efforts to establish justice despite any obstacles.

item.title: Pique says Owono's 12-match ban after De Miguel death is unfair
item.description:
FC Andorra's majority shareholder Gerard Pique criticised Jesus Owono's 12-match ban following a fatal collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, saying it unfairly blamed the goalkeeper for "consequences that were not his fault".
Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in a Spanish second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding heavily with De Miguel while trying to clear.
De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and died the next day, plunging football into shock and mourning.
In a video posted to TikTok late on Monday, former Spain and Barcelona great Pique said the Spanish football federation's punishment put Owono "in a situation that isn't fair".
"What it does is blame Jesus for consequences which were not his fault," Pique said in his first public comments on the decision.
"I think the punishment should be for the action, not for the consequences," added Pique, who compared the tragedy in Tenerife to a similar incident which led to a shorter ban.
Owono, 25, has said he is enduring the "hardest days of my life" after De Miguel's death, which Pique described as an "accident" that was "totally inexplicable".
FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said the goalkeeper will decide if and when he returns to football after the tragedy
"Jesus will need more than 12 games in order to be available and compete," said Pique.
"No suspension will bring Demi back to us," added Pique, referring to De Miguel by a popular nickname.
Spanish police sources have told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision, a standard procedure for unnatural deaths.

item.title: Ronaldo cloud still hangs over Portugal coach Jesus
item.description:
Portugal coach Jorge Jesus asked when he will stop being peppered with questions over Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement after a 4-1 defeat to Denmark sparked criticism from the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's mother.
Dolores Aveiro said she was glad to see Jesus suffer his first defeat since taking charge after the World Cup as Ronaldo had been "deceived" by the former Benfica boss.
"Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother?" Jesus asked ahead of Portugal's final Nations League group fixture away to Wales on Tuesday.
"I don't know when it is going to stop. If you guys ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer."
Ronaldo, 41, announced his international retirement earlier this month after a falling out with Jesus, who he also worked under at Saudi club Al-Nassr.
The ex-Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus star accused Jesus of broken promises after he was asked to warm up during a match against Norway in September without being introduced as a substitute.
Ronaldo left the team camp and was handed a 30-day suspension and token fine.
He apologised and was expected to return to the Portugal squad, but instead brought down the curtain on a 23-year international career.
His 234 appearances and 146 goals are both world records in the men's game.
But his lack of mobility was often pinpointed as a factor in a richly-talented Portugal squad falling short in recent major tournaments.
Jesus's side had made a perfect start with four consecutive wins prior to Saturday's shock defeat to the Danes.
"After the game against Denmark everyone is asking me about different individuals, not about the team or winning here," added Jesus.
"We played one bad game and it's harder to move on when we have a result like that, but we are going to try and win the game."
Portugal only need a point in Cardiff to secure top spot in Nations League group A4 against a Wales side that will finish bottom of the section.
"You were all having a go at him for playing, and then as soon as he retires, suddenly it's all hell breaking loose!" Wales boss Craig Bellamy told the Portuguese media.
"He is one of the best players that has ever played the game. We're all going to miss him."

item.title: French cricket 'dying' as federation crisis and chaos deepens
item.description:
Cricket in France is at risk of disappearing altogether, less than two years before the sport makes its long-awaited Olympic return.
The last, and only time that cricket was played at the Olympics was in Paris in 1900, where England beat France by 158 runs to win the gold medal.
France will not be at the Twenty20 tournament at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, and cricket in the country is on the verge of "dying" due to a crisis within the country's federation, Miriam Romero, a player and administrator, told AFP.
Clubs suspended the national league this year as they try to force president Prebagarane 'Prebou' Balane to resign following a series of scandals.
The organisation lost its recognition by France's sports ministry early this year, while the International Cricket Council (ICC) in June suspended development funding and placed France Cricket on notice for "non-compliance with membership criteria".
This came after scandals such as 'ghost' women's matches and development funding that was unaccounted for.
"We must not let cricket die in France, it's a shame," Romero, who is president of the Paris regional cricket committee, told AFP.
"If we don't do anything (it will die)."
Romero, who at 65 still plays, was previously on France Cricket's finance committee and is also a director at Paris Universitaire Club (PUC), one of the main cricket clubs in France.
She says PUC and other clubs have left France Cricket and are trying to set up a new national association to replace the existing structure.
Others, though, simply want Balane to resign so they can resolve the governance issues that saw them lose recognition from the ICC and the sports ministry.
According to the minutes of a board meeting in June, seen by the France 24 television station before it was deleted from the France Cricket website, Balane said he would resign on July 17.
But board member Jubaid Ahamed said Balane had not fulfilled his promise.
Despite repeated attempts by AFP to contact Balane and France Cricket, neither replied.
The chaos led the main clubs in France Cricket's domestic championship to suspend the competition in mid-August, meaning the season was never completed.
They have had enough and their demands are simple: "Firstly, to change the president. Then, to restructure France Cricket by implementing more flexible rules to develop youth and women's cricket," Djega Sankaran, the former president of the Morangis club, south of Paris, said.
He said he had resigned so he could speak freely without repercussions for his club.
AFP spoke to the president of the France Gymkhana club, Rizwan Babri, the president of another club and the team manager from a third club who all confirmed they wanted Balane to resign and for France Cricket to be restructured.
One person described Balane as acting like "God Almighty", another accused him of treating the federation as "his private affair".
In November, 34 clubs -- more than enough to reach the necessary one third threshold -- asked France Cricket for an extraordinary general meeting to submit a motion of no confidence in Balane and the executive committee, but the president refused, in email responses seen by AFP.
- 'Cry-babies' -
The crisis had been brewing for some time.
It began when France 24 broke an explosive story in 2023 about clubs in the country faking women's matches, apparently so France Cricket could benefit from hundreds of thousands of dollars of ICC funding.
The national women's cricket team wrote an open letter demanding an investigation and accountability, but instead, France Cricket suspended them.
"What was sad for us was that the men, the other clubs, did not support us," Sabine Lieury, a former French women's international and ex-president of Nantes Cricket Club, told AFP.
"The cricket world didn't want to rebel with the French girls to say that this was unacceptable."
Worst of all, the men's national team accused the women of being "cry-babies" and disloyal.
"No one did anything, they kept playing to protect themselves."
But they changed their tune after France Cricket lost its ICC development funding and French government recognition.
France Cricket have always denied that women's ghost matches took place -- Balane told the BBC in June that it had "never" happened. But that was not true. In fact, it was still happening last year.
The problem was that the federation obliged clubs to set up a women's team and threatened them with fines or even demotion if they did not fulfil fixtures.
Some clubs tried, but there was not the necessary interest to do so in such a tight timeframe.
"Everyone brought women's teams one way or another, with cousins, but it was just to avoid Prebou's sanctions," said Sankaran, who was heavily involved in trying to develop cricket in the Ile de France region around Paris.
"There were six people here, four people there. There were no (real) matches."
In the end, it was easier not to have a women's team.
"There were agreements between clubs: 'You won't get a fine and I won't get a fine'. They made up the scores," said Sankaran. "All the clubs made mistakes, me included."
- 'Not surprised' -
But those who were playing had always been suspicious.
There were four teams in the French women's first division at that time: Nantes, PUC, Lille and Lisses. But there were nine teams in the second division, and none were ever promoted.
"How is it that every year, we never see someone coming from these second division teams?" said Lieury.
"When the scandal broke, we were shocked, but at the same time, we said: 'we're not surprised, we've never seen these girls'."
Even in 2024 and 2025, only two clubs -- PUC and AC Stains -- could muster a full women's team and genuinely fulfil fixtures.
Tara Britton, a former Lisses and France player who subsequently joined PUC, said the only genuine match her new team played was against Stains.
The other teams either did not turn up, did so without enough players, or wanted to play with a tennis ball rather than a cricket ball.
The France Cricket website lists the results from 2024 and 2025 with PUC as the champions and Stains as the beaten "finalists".
But Britton said those seasons essentially amounted to a single match.
And then there is the question of the ICC development funding.
Numerous clubs told AFP that they never received any help from France Cricket. Sankaran said the organisation even refused to contribute to the purchase of a plastic wicket or cricket nets, offering only a loan instead.

item.title: Wirtz feels the fun as Germany run riot over Netherlands
item.description:
Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.
Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp's six-game stint as coach.
It was Germany's biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959.
"The game was outstanding," Klopp told German broadcaster ARD. "We scored unbelievable goals. It was just insane. A fantastic football match and a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have even dared to wish for all of this."
Klopp singled out Gruda and Scherhant, two players he has given their debuts, for special praise.
"Boy can those two play. But the amount of work they put in, it's immense. That's what defines a team -- and plenty of others can play football too."
So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany.
"We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half," Wirtz told ARD.
The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece's 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group.
The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany's second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will.
"I'm really sad, because before the game I was really proud," Xavi told reporters.
"Today it was not about the football, but about speed and about (our) values."
"I want to say sorry to our supporters, because today we showed our worst face. It's part of the process... We need to keep going and work on our values."
Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a "final."
The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward.
The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away.
Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post.
Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post.
"I don't think it could have gone any better, to score the opener here in my city. I don't think I could have dreamed of better -- it's unbelievable," Scherhant said.
The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc.
Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone.
RB Leipzig winger Gruda laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar.
In his first Germany match on home soil and just his second overall, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post.
"We don't mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz.
"We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team."

item.title: What issues do leaders face at the Apec summit?
item.description:
From nuclear weapons to artificial intelligence, world leaders will tackle a range of issues when they gather in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit this week.
With all eyes on a crowning trilateral meeting between US, Chinese and Russian leaders on Thursday, AFP takes a look at the topics that may be discussed:
Trade tensions will loom over the economic leaders’ meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday.
US President Donald Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on many countries, which China has met head-on with counter-levies and threats to withhold crucial exports.
On the sidelines of last year’s Apec summit in South Korea, Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping reached a tenuous truce in their trade war, but it will expire in January.
“The key overriding goal is to prevent another round of aggressive destabilizing tariffs and trade wars rather than to produce any single major milestone,” Dylan Loh, from Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University (NTU), told AFP.
The leaders’ “priority” would be “keeping the truce alive,” especially with another Trump-Xi meeting expected at the G20 summit in Miami in December, said Lizzi Lee, a fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute (Aspi).
Countries like Canada will also be looking to broaden their trade partnerships -- including with China -- to reduce dependence on the United States.
China has confirmed that Xi, Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin will meet on the sidelines of Apec on Thursday for their first trilateral summit.
Beijing has said the three leaders will discuss “safeguarding world peace,” but US officials say Trump is not expected to bring up Russia’s war in Ukraine.
Kyiv is concerned about being sidelined, with Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga saying a meeting between US, Chinese and Russian leaders would “only encourage Putin to continue this war”.
Beijing, insisting it is a neutral party, has never denounced the Russian invasion, and has instead called for peace talks.
“Beijing will remain respectful of Russia’s own aims in the war and balance that with growing calls from Europe to exert a little more influence in that regard,” NTU’s Loh said.
Putin would probably have the most to gain from the trilateral meeting, ASPI’s Lee added.
“Just being at the table with Trump and Xi would elevate Russia’s standing and potentially shift the conversation toward a broader great-power bargain over European security,” she said.
The Trump administration is keen to push for denuclearization at the summit, having criticized China’s rapidly expanding nuclear arsenal.
Analysts however, are sceptical that Trump, Putin and Xi can achieve a three-way deal to reduce arms.
“From Beijing’s perspective, the starting point is fundamentally unequal,” said Lee.
“The US and Russia have much larger arsenals, and China sees its own buildup as necessary for a credible deterrent.”
Washington has repeatedly accused China of conducting secret nuclear tests and demands that Beijing be part of any future arms control treaty.
The lapse in February of New Start -- the last treaty between top nuclear powers the United States and Russia -- presented the possibility of striking a “better agreement” including China, Washington said.
Beijing declined to join disarmament negotiations then.
Speculation has also been mounting of a potential meeting between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, with the US president having made repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks.
Countries have called for stronger governance and regulation of AI, as worries grow about its potential for military use and the risks posed by rogue autonomous-agent tools.
China-US talks could build on the AI “communication channel” agreed when Trump and Xi met in Washington in September.
“The next step should be to agree on what constitutes a reportable incident, who has authority to communicate, how quickly notifications must occur and how information can be verified without disclosing sensitive capabilities,” said Marina Zhang from the University of Technology Sydney.
Media reports have also suggested Xi, Putin and Trump may discuss the use of AI in nuclear weapons command systems.
Trump’s predecessor Joe Biden and Xi had agreed in 2024 that any decision to use nuclear weapons should be controlled by humans, not by AI, the White House said.
“There’s actually some common ground to build on,” Lee told AFP.
“(The) question is whether they can move beyond a general statement... toward something more practical.”
This would be a “much easier political sell” for Beijing than arms reductions, and “could give Trump something to announce without requiring anyone to compromise their nuclear posture,” she said.

item.title: Leaders, protesters greet Trump at Philippines summit
item.description:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday, where thousands of people protested his attendance at a regional summit he will seek to dominate after bruising election losses back home.
The president was greeted by a marching band and honor guard on the tarmac.
Some 13 kilometers (eight miles) away, 2,000 demonstrators faced off with police while carrying banners reading "Trump out now" and "Reject Pax Silica," a reference to a US supply chain initiative that has divided opinions in the Philippines.
The US president was to be flown immediately by helicopter to a meeting of the so-called Quad security alliance, with India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Japan's Sanae Takaichi and Australia's Anthony Albanese.
The gathering on the sidelines of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit is the Quad leaders' first since Trump's January 2025 return to power, and comes after his Republican party took a drubbing in this month's midterm elections.
While the Quad –- broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence -- has quietly progressed in deepening coordination, the short time allotted for Tuesday's meeting meant it was unlikely to extend beyond pleasantries, Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution told AFP.
The timing, however, carried significance, he said, given the historic meeting Trump will attend with China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin in just two days.
"It's a way of inoculating Trump against criticism of caving to authoritarians when he meets with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen," Hass said.
This would be the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China.
Hayley Channer, economic security director at the Sydney-based United States Studies Centre, said Trump's decision to include Asean on his travel agenda was noteworthy, as "Southeast Asia has never been a high priority for the United States."
Japan's foreign ministry said the Quad agenda would include discussions of the East and South China Sea -- areas where multiple parties have overlapping claims with China.
Trump will later attend a meeting with Asean heads of state before going to a gala dinner.
While Asean leaders have spent three days grappling with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump's ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a "countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism" while touting Beijing's own expanding trade with the bloc.
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada's Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market.
Trump's arrival comes on the heels of an announced US rules shift on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle Asean members.
Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion."
Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate "trusted access" for firms based in the city-state.
Trump is set to meet with Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to China's Shenzhen.
Channer, from the US Studies Centre, said the Manila visit was "likely because the US is trying to further its Pax Silica initiative, to build a complete mine-to-chip supply chain."
Aimed at countering China's dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines, as its flagship 1,620-hectare (about 4,000-acre) AI manufacturing hub north of Manila threatens to displace Indigenous families.
"We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people," Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday's protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words "Pax Silica Sashay Away!"
US Ambassador Lee Lipton, a Trump appointee, said last week that a long-rumored deal signing for the site would not take place during the president's visit.

item.title: Pakistan: Former leader Khan pleads for medical care
item.description:
Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan appealed to the country’s Supreme Court in a bid to receive urgent medical attention for himself and his wife.
According to an open letter conveyed to the court through Khan’s lawyer, the former leader’s doctors had warned him of a risk for brain hemorrhage and cardiac arrest and that his blood pressure had risen sharply.
He also said his wife Bushra Bibi required further eye operation, and that she is at risk of losing her eyesight should she not be granted the surgery.
The letter was released to the public by Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party and lawyer Salman Safdar.
“Today, I ask only that my wife and I be treated,” the letter reads, asking the judges to give him “justice” before it was too late.
“I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive,” Khan wrote.
An earlier court order ordered Khan’s transfer to a hospital in Pakistani capital Islamabad, with Khan alleging that the authorities had not implemented it.
However, cabinet minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said Khan was receiving medical care, while also receiving food and books of his liking.
According to Chaudhry, the former leader has been taken to medical examinations at a hospital in Islamabad eight times, with his health and blood pressure being found to be in order.
Despite being in prison since 2023 for corruption offenses, Khan is still considered a popular figure in Pakistan, with his party demanding his release. His wife is alo serving jail time for graft offenses.
Khan argues the charges against him are politically motivated, which the government denies.
The government, led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, also denied Khan was in solitary confinement. More than 900 visits to Khan have been registered since he started his jail time in 2023, according to the authorities.
In a previous case, Khan’s attorney told the court that his client had lost about 85% of his right eye’s vision. However, his sister later said his situation was improving.

item.title: Iran targets Bahrain as Mideast temperatures rise again
item.description:
Bahrain was targeted by a third Iranian drone attack in five days on Tuesday, raising temperatures in the Middle East war as the United States beefs up its military presence.
Explosions boomed across the tiny nation’s capital as a mobile-phone alert warned residents, shaken by the first attacks in the Gulf since September, to seek safety.
Bahrain’s armed forces said they “confronted, intercepted, and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives,” while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system.
“Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said.
The attack was in response to the “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones,” it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Bahrain, which hosts the US navy’s Fifth Fleet, was heavily targeted earlier in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. It had been peaceful for weeks until Iranian drone attacks on Friday and Sunday.
The latest attack came as the US moved the USS Theodore Roosevelt into the region, bringing the number of American carrier strike groups in the region to three.
The deployment adds to an already large US naval presence, which includes two other carriers -- the George H.W. Bush and the George Washington -- and more than a dozen destroyers.
Drone attacks have resumed ahead of this week’s unprecedented trilateral summit between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts.
Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will discuss “world peace” at the talks in Shenzhen, according to China. Trump has said he plans to discuss the Iran war at the meeting.
Also on Tuesday, Iran rebuked Bahrain over Monday’s sentencing of 64 Shia Muslims to life in prison on terror charges, calling it a “violation of human rights” and denying any links to the defendants.
Rattled by the fresh attacks, Bahrainis spoke of their longing for quieter times in the energy-rich Gulf, previously renowned as a haven of security in the volatile region.
“I was on my way to work when the warning sirens went on,” Abdulrahman Abdullah, a Bahraini civil servant in his forties, told AFP.
“Absolutely, fear and anxiety rise as attacks increase and there are blasts. We hope things will go back to how they were and we will enjoy security and peace in the region.”
Another Bahraini civil servant, Lulwa Mahmoud, told AFP she is “caught in a cycle of anxiety” about the war.
Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy Mena Analytica called the flare-up a “deliberate testing of boundaries rather than an immediate return to full-scale warfare.”
“Both Washington and Tehran are pushing the envelope, probing each other’s red lines and trying to establish how far they can escalate without provoking a response that spirals beyond their control.”
“Bahrain is particularly significant because Iran is demonstrating that the costs of American military action need not remain confined to Iranian territory,” he added.
“Bahrain is the most vulnerable because of its geographic exposure,” said Krieg. “It has no strategic depth and all high value targets are concentrated in a small geographic area.”
Since September, the conflict had mainly been restricted to the area around the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with the US blockading Iranian ports and Tehran attempting to control the oil shipping route.
Tehran has insisted that Washington meet conditions including the release of frozen assets abroad, sanctions relief and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports in exchange for reopening the strait.
Trump’s Republican Party suffered major losses in midterm congressional elections that both the president and Vice President JD Vance blamed on the Iran war, which has sharply driven up prices and is widely unpopular in the United States.
Washington has appeared to dial back threats of renewed strikes in the wake of the midterms, but Trump said last week that a deal with Iran on ending the war was unnecessary.

item.title: Taliban supreme leader makes rare visit to Afghan capital
item.description:
The Taliban’s reclusive Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada made a rare visit to the Afghan capital Kabul on Tuesday, heralding the “extraordinary turn of events” that brought him to power.
Based in Kandahar, the southern heartland of the Taliban movement, Akhundzada has ruled Afghanistan by decree for more than five years.
“Now that Islam has triumphed, an Islamic system has been established, and the Islamic Emirate holds authority -- it is essential to help people understand the true nature of the Islamic Emirate” of Afghanistan, Akhundzada said at Kabul University, according to a government live audio feed.
Akhundzada inherited the Taliban leadership a decade ago and has made only a handful of visits to Kabul in recent years.
A massive security operation was launched ahead of his attendance at the Kabul conference, about the impact of his decrees, with heavily-manned checkpoints installed around the venue.
AFP journalists saw snipers atop buildings surrounding Kabul University, dozens of Humvees guarding the gates and intelligence agents stationed in the area.
Kabul University has been shut since Sunday, staff and students told AFP, while residents in the area said their homes were searched.
The thousands of attendees included senior officials and scholars, the Ministry of Higher Education said Monday.

item.title: PM urges students to be responsible citizens
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged students to look beyond academic studies and take an active interest in sports, arts, culture and the history of the country, stressing the importance of becoming responsible citizens.
He also advised them to be conscious of their responsibilities towards themselves, society, the environment and the country.
The prime minister made the remarks on Tuesday when 50 GPA-5 achievers from three schools in Nawabganj, Dhaka, met him at the parliament.
The schools are Kalakopa High School, Bandura Holy Cross High School and College, and St Euphrasia's Girls' High School and College.
Addressing the students, Tarique said they would eventually complete their studies and pursue different professions, including medicine, engineering, law, science and teaching.
Regardless of their chosen professions, he said, they must always remain mindful of their responsibilities towards society and the country.
The prime minister said every individual has responsibilities not only towards themselves but also towards the people around them, society and the environment.
He stressed that people must act responsibly towards the state, society and the environment as conscientious citizens.
He said everyone could contribute to the welfare of society through sincere efforts from their respective positions.
Emphasising the importance of extracurricular activities, Tarique told the students: “Alongside your studies, you must also take part in sports. You should also learn about art and culture. You need to know about the history of your country and other relevant subjects.”
He said education should not be limited to memorising lessons and achieving good results in examinations, as there was much more to learn beyond academic curricula.
Gaining knowledge in different fields, he added, would enrich their lives and help them grow into well-rounded individuals.

item.title: Duchess of Coimbra honours Sabur Khan during DIU visit
item.description:
A member of the Portuguese Royal Family, Maria Francisca de Bragança, Duchess of Coimbra, visited Daffodil International University (DIU) in Savar on Tuesday, where she presented the university chairman, Dr Md Sabur Khan, with the ‘Knight of the Crown Royal’ honor.
The recognition makes Dr Sabur Khan the first person from Bangladesh to receive the honor. He was also recognized as the Ambassador of the Fair Pay Charter in Bangladesh.
The Duchess was accompanied by the Duke of Coimbra, Duarte Maria de Sousa Araújo Martins, and an international delegation from Portugal and the United Kingdom, including representatives of the Global Fair Pay Charter and London Tea Exchange.
During the visit, the delegation explored the academic and infrastructural facilities of Daffodil Smart City and learned about the university's educational, research, innovation and technology initiatives. The Duchess and Dr Sabur Khan also jointly participated in a commemorative tree-planting program.
A special reception was organized at the university's International Conference Hall, where DIU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr M R Kabir delivered the welcome address. Dr Sabur Khan and Sir Sheikh Aliur Rahman, head of the international delegation, also addressed the gathering.
In her remarks, the Duchess shared her experience of visiting the university and emphasized the importance of international connections, cultural exchange and mutual cooperation.
Another highlight of the visit was the inauguration of ‘Cozinha Real – The Royal Lounge’, a new facility of DIU's Department of Tourism and Hospitality Management. The lounge is also expected to promote cultural exchange between Bangladesh and Portugal through their respective food traditions and hospitality practices.

item.title: Bringing Bangladesh's literary voices to the world
item.description:
South Asian Literature in Translation (SALT) at the University of Chicago and the Department of English and Humanities (ENH) at BRAC University are jointly organizing a three-day residential workshop on literary translation in Bangladesh, bringing together translators and literary professionals in Savar from Monday to Wednesday.
The workshop focuses on Bangladesh's diverse languages and literary traditions, exploring how translation can help local writers reach international audiences and make their works accessible beyond their original linguistic communities.
Three experienced literary translators are facilitating the workshop: Daniel Hahn, OBE, Jason Grunebaum and Shabnam Nadiya.
The program began with plenary sessions and discussions led by Hahn and Nadiya. Speaking about the practice of literary translation, Nadiya said, “Translation is a creative work that requires meticulous and consistent practice.”
Hahn is a writer, editor and translator known for his work with Latin American fiction. He is currently co-editing The Penguin Book of Brazilian Short Stories with Padma Viswanathan.
Grunebaum, co-director of SALT, teaches Hindi language and literary translation at the University of Chicago. His translations include works by Uday Prakash and Manzoor Ahtesham, and he has received several translation fellowships and awards.
Nadiya, a Philadelphia-based writer and translator, has introduced works by several Bangladeshi authors to English-speaking audiences. Her translations include Mashiul Alam's The Meat Market: Ten Stories and a Novella, Leesa Gazi's Hellfire and Shaheen Akhtar's Beloved Rongomala.
As part of the program, Hahn will deliver a public lecture at BRAC University's campus on November 19 at 3:30pm. The lecture is open to anyone interested in literature and translation.
The initiative comes amid growing discussions about the international circulation of literature and the role of English-language publishing in shaping which literary voices reach global readers. Despite its relatively small geographical size, Bangladesh is home to multiple languages and diverse literary traditions, making translation an important means of expanding their reach.

item.title: How gel polish works, how to remove it safely
item.description:
Regular nail polish rarely lasts long. Exposure to water, a little carelessness, or everyday household chores can cause the color to chip around the edges within just two or three days, leaving nails looking untidy. To avoid the hassle of frequently reapplying or changing nail color, gel polish has emerged as a popular alternative.
Many people confuse gel polish with nail extensions, although the two are entirely different procedures. So, what makes gel polish different, and why is it becoming a preferred choice for nail enthusiasts?.
According to experts, nail extensions involve artificially lengthening short nails to achieve a desired size and shape. Gel polish, on the other hand, does not change the length or shape of natural nails. Instead, it involves applying a long-lasting coating of color, glitter, or intricate designs over the natural nails.
Unlike regular nail polish, which dries when exposed to air and is generally short-lived, gel polish is made with a specialized chemical formula that requires curing under a dedicated LED lamp. The polish is applied in layers, with each layer exposed to the light for a specific period to harden and set.
Experts say gel polish can remain intact for one to one-and-a-half months, depending on the natural growth of the nails. Even when exposed to stains from turmeric or spices during cooking, the polish retains its glossy appearance, and stains can be removed with a swipe of regular nail polish remover.
This makes gel polish a convenient and time-saving option for those who want their nails to look well-groomed without having to reapply color frequently.
1. Shaping and preparation
The process begins by shaping the nails according to the client's preference. Popular options include oval, square and coffin shapes.
The cuticles are then cleaned using a buffer, and the nail surface is prepared for color application and nail art with specialized sanitizing products.
2. Applying the base coat and color
A base coat is applied first to help the gel polish adhere firmly to the nails. The chosen gel color or nail art design is then carefully applied.
3. Curing under LED light
After each coat is applied, the nails are placed under an LED lamp for around 60 to 90 seconds to cure and harden the gel.
4. Applying the top coat
Finally, a top coat is applied to seal the design and provide additional protection. The nails are then placed under the lamp again for approximately two minutes to complete the process.
The result is a smooth, glass-like finish with a lasting shine.
Farhana Samad emphasizes that certain precautions are essential when using gel polish, particularly when it comes to removing it.
1. Avoid peeling or picking it off
As natural nails grow, a gap may appear near the cuticles. However, pulling, peeling, or biting off the polish is not advisable, as doing so can damage the natural layers of the nails.
2. Have it removed by a professional
Gel polish cannot be removed in the same way as regular nail polish. It requires specialized products and a proper removal process, which can take some time. Therefore, it is best to seek assistance from an experienced professional. Ideally, customers should return to the salon where the polish was originally applied.
3. Choose a reputable salon
Using substandard products or getting the procedure done by an inexperienced technician can leave nails thin and brittle. Choosing a reputable salon with trained professionals and quality products is therefore essential for maintaining healthy nails.

item.title: Want to eat rice with fewer calories?
item.description:
Many people remain concerned about excess weight, making healthy eating habits an important part of weight management. However, for rice-loving populations such as Bangladeshis, reducing calorie intake can be particularly challenging, as rice is a staple food and a major source of carbohydrates.
But what if a simple change in the way rice is cooked could reduce the calories it provides?
According to a recent study, a small cooking trick involving coconut oil and refrigeration may help reduce the amount of digestible starch in rice, potentially lowering its calorie content.
Rice is rich in carbohydrates, which are broken down into glucose during digestion to provide the body with energy. When the body does not use this energy, excess glucose may be stored, potentially contributing to weight gain over time.
Researchers have explored a simple method that could make rice a more calorie-conscious food choice.
The process involves adding a tablespoon of coconut oil to boiling water before adding the rice. The rice is then cooked for approximately 25 minutes. Once cooked, the excess water is drained, and the rice is refrigerated for some time.
This method is believed to increase the amount of resistant starch in rice. Unlike ordinary starch, resistant starch is not fully broken down and absorbed in the small intestine. As a result, the body may absorb fewer calories from it.
According to the research cited, this cooking technique could reduce the digestible calorie content of rice by up to 60%.
However, the actual reduction may vary depending on the type of rice, cooking method, and refrigeration conditions. While this technique may help reduce the digestibility of starch, it should not be considered a substitute for balanced eating habits and regular physical activity.

item.title: Workers block Dhaka-Mymensingh highway over wage demands
item.description:
Garment workers staged protests and blocked several points along the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in Gazipur on Tuesday, demanding higher wages.
The workers began marching from Bhabanipur in Gazipur Sadar upazila at around 12:15pm, targeting the gates of several garment factories along the highway. The protests prompted around 70 factories to suspend operations for the day.
The workers blocked the highway at several points, including Bagher Bazar, Memberbari, Shirirchala and Gargariya Masterbari in Sreepur, bringing traffic to a standstill.
Police intervened after receiving reports of the unrest, dispersing the protesters and using sound grenades to bring the situation under control. After repeated attempts to block the highway, the workers eventually cleared the road after 2:30pm. Traffic has since returned to normal, although movement remains slow.
Factories that suspended operations included Hoplon Apparels Ltd, Masco Cotton Ltd, Masco Tex Ltd, Masco G-1, Masco G-2, Jarms Industries Ltd, Base Fashion, Kai Aluminium, EH Fabrics, GJ Caps, Oishi Fashion Ltd, Tanaz Fashion, Viyellatex, Setan-2, Deoti Fashion, GJ Fashion, Denim Fashion, SS Sweater, Sancheri Body Fashion Ltd, Mick Sweater Ltd, Lujin Fashion Ltd, Cotton Clothing Ltd, Masco Embroidery Ltd, TMSS Apparels Ltd, TPO Garments, Spirit Garments, CVU Garments, Parkview Garments, TJ Sweater, Reolife Ltd, Sunny Sweater, RG Apparels Ltd, Trouser Land, Orient Sweater, Lucky Star Garments, MHC Apparels Ltd, HBS Garments, Royal Footwear, SK Trim Garments, Ripon Garments, AEC Apparels Ltd, G & Fashion Ltd, KA Design, New RG, Tosuka Apparels Ltd, Cotton Clothing BD Ltd, Marchstis Garments, Azam Foot, Eco Tex Ltd, Masco Pikasu Garments and Antas Design Ltd.
The list also includes Concept Knitting Ltd, Mim Fashion Ltd, Baraka Fashion Ltd, Billa Trade Ltd, D.H. Global Ltd, Knit Bazar Ltd, Tamisna Apparels Ltd and Panacea Fashionwear Ltd in the Tongi and Bhabanipur areas.
Other affected factories included Fakira Garments and RMG Garments, both part of the NAZ Group; Mondol Intimates Garments and Golden Refit Garments in Bagher Bazar; Esrotex Garments in Notun Bazar; MHC Garments in Sreepur; and the Subline garment factory of Meghna Group.

“They were promptly cleared from the highway, and traffic has since returned to normal, although movement remains slow,” he said.

item.title: Portuguese princess visiting Bangladesh
item.description:
A prominent member of Portugal’s historic royal family, Infanta Maria Francisca, duchess of coimbra (Portuguese princess), is visiting Bangladesh from Monday to November 24.
As a member of the House of Braganza, she is actively involved in social, cultural and humanitarian initiatives in Portugal and across Europe.
The visit brings together three important connections - royal heritage, Fair Pay and Bangladesh’s tea - and will provide an international platform for the heritage and global potential of Sylhet Tea, said a media release.
She will join the official launch of Sylhet Tea, London Tea Exchange’s new tea collection featuring premium teas from Sylhet, Bangladesh. The event will be held on Wednesday.
On the last International Tea Day, Braganza Blend, from the Sylhet Tea collection, was presented as the Portuguese Royal Family’s official tea.
The launch in Bangladesh will mark the beginning of Sylhet Tea’s journey into the global market, highlighting the heritage and international potential of Sylhet’s tea.
She is particularly known for her public engagements and charitable activities. During her visit to Bangladesh, she will take part in a number of cultural, social and humanitarian engagements.
A key purpose of her visit is to support the Global Fair Pay Charter, an international initiative founded by Sir Sheikh Aliur Rahman OBE, group chairman of London Tea Exchange, which promotes fair and dignified pay for workers around the world.
The initiative has received support from the United Nations, the Commonwealth, C40 and other international organisations, with Bangladesh emerging as an important partner.
The princess is also accompanied by several Global Ambassadors for Fair Pay, including representatives associated with Portugal, China and Pakistan.
Their participation will bring together international voices in support of fair pay, social responsibility and international cooperation.

item.title: Political theatrics, asylum claims and the cost to British Bangladeshis
item.description:
The violent street fighting between Awami League and National Citizen Party (NCP) activists in Romford, east London, on November 16 has exposed an uncomfortable reality: political rivalries imported from Bangladesh are damaging the reputation of the wider British Bangladeshi community.
The confrontation erupted on a road behind Mayfair Hall following a reception for NCP Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam MP.
The fighting reportedly continued for around 20 minutes, leaving several people injured and requiring police intervention.
According to eyewitness accounts, local Awami League activists initiated the confrontation, catching NCP supporters off guard.
Protesters allegedly threw eggs and water bottles at arriving guests and assaulted attendees outside the venue.
Nahid himself avoided direct confrontation, having entered the hall several hours before the program and departed through a rear exit.
British emergency services confirmed responding to the disorder.
The London Ambulance Service treated six people at the scene, while police reported that three were taken to hospital.
Yet the consequences of this confrontation extend far beyond those directly involved.
For British Bangladeshis who have spent generations building their lives in the United Kingdom, such incidents turn community spaces into battlegrounds for political rivalries originating thousands of miles away.
Community observers have described the Romford confrontation as an example of staged political provocation rather than genuine democratic engagement.
The concern is that some activists may deliberately create confrontations to attract publicity, demonstrate loyalty to political leaders or strengthen their political standing.
More controversially, allegations have circulated that certain individuals participate in such clashes to generate police reports, medical records and photographs that could support applications for political asylum in Britain.
These allegations require independent investigation.
There is no verified evidence that the Romford confrontation was organised for asylum purposes, and genuine asylum claims must not be confused with allegations of deliberate political manipulation.
Nevertheless, the question deserves scrutiny.
If political violence is being manufactured for personal advantage, it undermines both legitimate democratic activism and public confidence in the asylum system.
Political loyalty, personal ambition or immigration considerations cannot justify turning British streets into arenas of intimidation and violence.
The immediate consequence of the Romford disorder was its exploitation by British anti-immigration voices.
Political figures associated with Reform UK used the confrontation to criticise immigration policies and portray the violence as an example of foreign political disputes being imported into Britain.
Such reactions demonstrate how quickly the conduct of a small group can become a damaging narrative about an entire community.
When videos of Bangladeshi men fighting circulate across social media without context, the consequences are not confined to the participants.
Families, shopkeepers, students and professionals in London, Luton, Birmingham and Oldham may find themselves facing suspicion because of political conflicts they neither support nor participate in.
For generations, British Bangladeshis have worked to establish themselves within British society.
Their contributions to business, education, culture and public life should not be overshadowed by the actions of political activists seeking attention or confrontation.
Yet every incident of this kind risks reinforcing damaging stereotypes and weakening the community’s standing.
The reputational cost is collective, even when responsibility for the violence is individual.
The deeper tragedy is how much energy some sections of the British Bangladeshi community continue to devote to Bangladesh’s domestic political rivalries instead of constructive engagement with British public life.
Anyone who makes Britain their home has opportunities to participate in mainstream politics, influence local councils, shape public policy and contribute to national democratic institutions.
Communities of Indian and Pakistani heritage have established substantial political influence in Britain, including representation in Parliament, ministerial positions and important policymaking roles.
British Bangladeshis have also achieved political representation and made significant contributions.
Nevertheless, there remains considerable scope to strengthen their influence across politics, business and wider public life.
That progress requires sustained civic participation, not street confrontations over political disputes in Dhaka.
While others are building influence within Westminster and local government, why should sections of the British Bangladeshi community remain preoccupied with factional battles that offer little benefit to their families or future generations?
Political differences are natural, and expatriates have every right to remain engaged with Bangladesh’s affairs.
But there is a fundamental difference between peaceful political participation and importing hostility into the streets of another country.
The former strengthens democracy. The latter damages public trust.
The Romford incident has drawn strong criticism from British Bangladeshi residents and community figures.
British Bangladeshi resident Farzana Boby Amie described the violence as disgusting and deeply shameful, stressing that political differences could never justify aggression, intimidation or physical confrontation.
Cultural organiser Mahbubur Rahman Shiblu similarly expressed concern that bringing Bangladesh’s political hostility into Britain was damaging the country’s reputation and leaving ordinary British Bangladeshis to bear the consequences.
Their frustration reflects a wider concern that community events are increasingly becoming opportunities for confrontation rather than dialogue.
The incident also disrupted Nahid Islam’s week-long visit to the United Kingdom, which began on November 13 and was scheduled to conclude on November 21.
Following the confrontation, his planned appearance on a local Bengali television channel was reportedly cancelled after Awami League activists gathered outside the station.
He also visited injured attendees at King’s College Hospital.
Such disruptions illustrate how political hostility can extend beyond individual events, affecting community engagement and the freedom to participate in political discussions.
British Bangladeshis have established roots in the United Kingdom over more than a century, with many families now in their fourth generation.
Yet questions remain about whether the community has fully realised its potential in mainstream politics, the economy and public life compared with other established South Asian communities.
These questions deserve serious reflection, not another round of political blame.
The younger generation needs successful role models, greater opportunities and a community whose public identity is defined by achievement rather than confrontation.
Instead, repeated political clashes risk leaving children and young people to inherit reputational damage created by disputes in which they had no involvement.
Why should an entire community suffer humiliation because some individuals cannot separate political allegiance from public responsibility?
Those determined to pursue Bangladesh’s party politics should do so through legitimate democratic channels, rather than turning British neighbourhoods into battlegrounds.
Nor should political confrontations become instruments for personal publicity, questionable asylum-related ambitions or hopes of securing a party leader’s favour and a future parliamentary nomination.
Such motives must be established through evidence before being attributed to individuals. But the wider principle is beyond dispute: political ambitions cannot justify violence or the collective embarrassment of a community.
British Bangladeshis should not have to defend their reputation every time rival political activists exchange blows on a London street.
The community has invested generations in building its future in Britain. That future must not be sacrificed for political theatrics rooted in conflicts thousands of miles away.
Enough humiliation has already been inflicted in the name of politics. There is no reason to pass more of it on to the next generation.

item.title: Arson, attacks beyond Dhaka fuel fears of fresh political unrest
item.description:
Political violence and sabotage spread beyond Dhaka on Tuesday, with attacks on a police station and a BNP lawmaker’s home in Gopalganj, and a road blockade and arson in Faridpur that left a Krishak Dal leader dead.
Several buses were also set on fire and crude bombs exploded at different locations in the capital. The circulation of an alleged audio clip featuring provocative remarks by a former minister now abroad has further fuelled political tension, raising fears of fresh unrest.
The country has been witnessing heightened political tensions for more than a month, with reports of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson almost daily.
In the audio clip circulated on social media on Tuesday, a voice is heard calling for two or three houses to be set on fire in every union and suggesting assault and killing if necessary. The remarks appear to target the ruling BNP and the National Citizen Party (NCP). The authenticity of the recording has not been established.
Around 9pm on Tuesday, activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League allegedly blocked the Dhaka-Barisal highway in Pukuria, Bhanga, Faridpur, and set fire to three motorcycles. Krishak Dal leader Raju Molla died after suffering severe burns.
Earlier, around 8:30pm, unidentified people set fire to the former residence of former Liberation War Affairs minister AKM Mozammel Haque in Gazipur. In Gopalganj, Awami League and Chhatra League activists allegedly vandalised and set fire to the home of BNP lawmaker SM Jilani, representing Gopalganj-3.
Attackers also set fire to Tungipara Police Station after making announcements over mosque loudspeakers. Clashes broke out between police and the attackers, leaving several police personnel injured. Earlier in the day, a group chanting slogans in support of the Awami League allegedly attacked and vandalised a BNP leader’s business establishment in Chittagong’s Khatunganj.
The incidents have prompted questions about whether the country is heading towards another period of political instability and how the ruling BNP and the NCP, which emerged from the July uprising, will respond.
Leaders from both parties said they primarily planned to keep their activists engaged in regular political programmes in December. They said the administration should deal with attempts to create disorder, while the parties would consider political programmes depending on developments.
Political leaders and analysts have warned that a failure by political parties to act responsibly could disrupt the democratic process and create an anarchic situation. They have urged all sides to exercise restraint.
Former Communist Party of Bangladesh general secretary Ruhin Hossain Prince said any provocative remarks encouraging violence were unacceptable, if the audio clip was genuine. However, he cautioned against political parties taking matters into their own hands, saying law enforcement agencies should handle attempts at sabotage.
Workers Party General Secretary Saiful Haque also condemned any alleged incitement to violence. He said the BNP and NCP could organise constructive programmes to prevent sabotage, but all parties must remain tolerant to preserve a healthy political environment.
Political analyst and writer Mahiuddin Ahmed said it was too early to determine whether the current situation would lead to further clashes.
The NCP has not announced any special programme to counter the activities of any particular political group in December. Its leaders said the party would focus on its scheduled programmes, including Victory Day celebrations, rather than taking to the streets in response to the actions of others.
NCP Joint Convener and Political Council member Sarwar Tushar said maintaining law and order was the administration’s responsibility, not the party’s.
He said the public would resist those attempting to create disorder if they crossed the limits.
The BNP has already instructed its leaders and activists to remain active alongside the administration to counter attempts to destabilise the country.
Acting BNP Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said on Sunday that party activists and those of its associate organisations would remain active in neighbourhoods to prevent sabotage.
A BNP joint secretary general, speaking on condition of anonymity, said party activists were holding meetings and rallies across the country and informing the administration about suspected acts of sabotage.
BNP Vice-Chairman Shamsuzzaman Dudu said the administration was responsible for controlling sabotage, but the party would remain active to protect public safety and maintain a normal political environment.
He said the party had planned peaceful programmes around Victory Day and the death anniversary of former prime minister Khaleda Zia in December, while maintaining a firm stance against violence.
Speaking at a programme at Rajshahi University on Tuesday, Rizvi said attempts were being made to return to power through crude bomb blasts, arson attacks on buses and attacks on police boxes. However, he said such incidents would not derail the country's democratic journey.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed addressed the attack on Tungipara Police Station, urging residents of Gopalganj not to fall for provocations allegedly coming from across the border.
He said the government had refrained from ordering a forceful response despite having police, Border Guard Bangladesh and other security personnel deployed near the area, as it wanted to avoid casualties.
The minister warned that those involved in the attack on the police station, assaults on law enforcement personnel, arson and acts of sabotage would be identified through video footage, audio recordings and photographs and brought to justice.

item.title: Home minister: Awami League to become ‘Tungipara Limited’
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has warned that the activities-banned Awami League will eventually become “Tungipara Limited”, vowing action against those involved in recent attacks in Gopalganj while ruling out the use of excessive force.
Speaking during a discussion in parliament on Tuesday night, he said the government would rather exercise patience in bringing 10 criminals to justice than risk shooting an innocent person.
His remarks came after Opposition Leader Dr Shafiqur Rahman raised concerns over attacks, arson, looting of firearms and the siege of Tungipara Police Station in Gopalganj.
Shafiqur said he had received information about plans for major acts of sabotage in the district ahead of Thursday. He urged the government to take effective steps to protect lives, property and state institutions, warning that unrest in Gopalganj could threaten security across the southwestern region.
In response, Salahuddin accused Awami League leaders and activists of encouraging arson from across the border. He said the government would not follow the party’s alleged repressive tactics.
The minister said law enforcement agencies would take lawful action if police stations or lawmakers’ homes were attacked. He added that video footage, audio recordings and photographs of those who allegedly incited the attack on Tungipara Police Station were available and would be used to identify and prosecute those involved.
He also urged residents of Gopalganj not to fall for provocations.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Barrister Andaleeve Rahman Partho said the recent activities in Gopalganj were aimed at drawing political attention and rallying Awami League activists.

item.title: Awami League activists torch police station, BNP MP’s house in Gopalganj
item.description:
Activists of the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations allegedly stormed Tungipara Police Station in Gopalganj on Tuesday evening, vandalised the premises, set fire to police vehicles and subsequently torched the residence of BNP lawmaker SM Jilani, triggering widespread panic and fresh concerns over the deteriorating security situation.
The violence erupted around 7:30pm after police detained several suspected Chhatra League activists, prompting hundreds of Awami League supporters to surround the police station and demand their release.
According to police and local witnesses, the protesters, many carrying sticks, overwhelmed police resistance, entered the station compound and set fire to vehicles and parts of the premises.
Witnesses also reported that the attackers freed the detained activists, although police had not independently confirmed their escape.
Police reportedly fired tear gas shells, rubber bullets and sound grenades to disperse the crowd, leading to clashes and chases.
Several people were reportedly injured, but their number and condition could not immediately be confirmed.
A short while later, another group of alleged Chhatra League activists attacked and set fire to the house of SM Jilani, the BNP lawmaker representing Gopalganj-3, comprising Tungipara and Kotalipara.
Tungipara Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mohammad Didarul Alam confirmed the attack on the lawmaker’s residence.
Witnesses said the attackers chanted slogans supporting the Awami League and Sheikh Hasina during the violence.
According to local sources, the confrontation began after police detained several Chhatra League activists near the upazila parishad while they were having tea.
The detainees were taken to Tungipara Police Station, prompting supporters to mobilise through loudspeaker announcements and gather outside the facility.
As the crowd grew, protesters attempted to enter the police station, leading to clashes with law enforcement personnel.
Police reportedly fired several rounds and used crowd-control equipment before retreating amid the confrontation.
Videos circulating on Facebook appeared to show at least three vehicles burning inside the station compound, while protesters shouted slogans and vandalised property.
In one Facebook Live broadcast, an individual identified as HM Rubel Farazi was heard threatening to set the police station on fire.
The authenticity and full circumstances of the footage could not immediately be independently verified.
Police Headquarters spokesperson Kamarum Munira confirmed around 9:10pm that Tungipara Police Station had been attacked and set on fire.
She said police had also received reports of vehicles being torched.
Earlier, Police Headquarters DIG (Crime and Operations) Mohammed Abu Sufian said authorities were gathering information after receiving reports that the station had been surrounded.
Eskandar Sheikh, acting station officer of Tungipara Fire Service, said firefighters had received reports of fires near the police station, Chourangi intersection and Bashbaria.
However, fire crews were unable to reach the affected locations because of security concerns.
He said firefighters would proceed once adequate protection was provided by law enforcement agencies.
Meanwhile, Awami League supporters reportedly erected barricades at Khalek Bazar, Patgati intersection, Barni and other points along roads connecting Gopalganj and Tungipara, disrupting traffic.
The latest attacks followed several days of unrest in Gopalganj, where activities-banned Awami League supporters staged armed processions, vandalised public property and reopened party offices.
Authorities had deployed additional security personnel and transferred the district’s deputy commissioner, superintendent of police and three officers-in-charge following Sunday’s violence.

item.title: Krishak Dal leader burnt to death during Awami Leaue blockade in Faridpur
item.description:
A local Krishak Dal leader died after being severely burned when three motorcycles were set on fire during a road blockade on the Dhaka-Barisal highway in Faridpur’s Bhanga Upazila on Tuesday night.
The incident took place around 9pm in the Pukuria area. The deceased, Raju Molla, was the joint organising secretary of Bhanga Upazila Krishak Dal and the son of Muktar Molla of Bakpura village.
Bhanga Upazila BNP President Khandaker Iqbal Hossain Selim alleged that activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League blocked the road, set fire to several motorcycles and attacked Raju before setting him on fire.
According to eyewitnesses and local sources, Raju sustained critical burn injuries and was taken to Bhanga Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead.
Health complex physician Tanzirul Islam Mamun said Raju was brought to the hospital around 9:30pm. Much of his body below the waist had been burned, he added.
Following the blockade and arson, local BNP activists went to the scene and, with police assistance, cleared the road and restored traffic. They also staged an immediate protest over Raju’s death.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Special Branch) Raihan Gafur said police had brought the situation under control after reaching the scene. Police were working to identify those involved, he added.

item.title: Crude bombs explode at five locations in Mohammadpur
item.description:
Crude bombs exploded at five locations in the capital’s Mohammadpur area on Tuesday night, while police detained one person in connection with the incidents.
Police said the explosions took place between 8:30pm and 10pm.
The first blast was reported in front of Krishi Market around 8:30pm, followed by explosions in Asad Gate, beside the SRB-2 camp in Basila and near Residential Model College.
A crude bomb was also thrown at the Tejgaon Deputy Commissioner’s Office but did not explode. A bomb disposal team later defused it.
Tejgaon Deputy Commissioner of Police Ibn-e-Mizan confirmed the incidents, saying legal action would be taken.
