item.title: Sayeed Khokon placed on 7-day remand in teenager murder case
item.description:
A Dhaka court has placed former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) mayor Sayeed Khokon on a seven-day remand for questioning in a case filed over the murder of teenager Abdul Motaleb in the capital’s Dhanmondi area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mehedi Hasan passed the order on Tuesday, following a petition filed by the investigation officer.
Inspector Sujan Haque of the Detective Branch (DB) police’s Ramna Zonal Team, who is investigating the case, had sought a 10-day remand for Khokon.
Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi argued in favour of the remand on behalf of the state, while senior lawyer Abu Sayeed Sagor, representing Khokon, opposed the plea and sought his bail.
According to the case statement, Motaleb was shot dead on August 4, 2024 while taking part in a procession near Zigatola Bus Stand during the July uprising.
On August 26, 2024, following the fall of the Awami League government, his father Abdul Matin filed a murder case with Dhanmondi Police Station.
The case names 176 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal and former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader. Khokon is listed as the 29th accused in the FIR.
Khokon, son of former undivided Dhaka City Corporation mayor Mohammad Hanif, was elected DSCC mayor in 2015. He was denied the Awami League's nomination in the subsequent mayoral election.
He later contested the 12th parliamentary election with the party's nomination and was elected MP from the Dhaka-6 constituency.
He was detained from a residence in Baridhara around 7am on Tuesday. SRB later handed him over to the Detective Branch (DB) of police.

item.title: NCC Bank to finance export-oriented frozen food sector
item.description:
NCC Bank PLC has signed a participation agreement with Bangladesh Bank under its Tk2,000 crore pre-finance fund for the export-oriented frozen food sector, to promote the country's frozen food industry, diversify exports, and expand financing facilities for entrepreneurs engaged in this sector.
In the presence of Arief Hossain Khan, executive director of Bangladesh Bank, Md Zakir Anam, additional managing director of NCC Bank, and AKM Sayduzzaman, director of Bangladesh Bank, signed and exchanged the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Among others, Muhammad Ansarul Kabir, additional director of Bangladesh Bank; Ahsan Tariq, SEVP and head of RMG & export cell of NCC Bank; and Mohammed Abul Kalam Azad, VP of rmg & export cell of NCC Bank, along with senior officials from both organizations, were present at the event.
The export-oriented frozen food industry is one of the country's promising sectors, offering significant opportunities to expand exports of frozen shrimp, fish, fishery products, and other frozen food items in international markets.
To ensure necessary financial support for entrepreneurs and facilitate production and business operations in this sector, Bangladesh Bank has established the Tk2,000 crore pre-finance fund from its own resources.
Under this fund, eligible entrepreneurs and export-oriented enterprises will receive financing facilities for the production, procurement, processing, and preservation of frozen shrimp, fish, fishery products, and other frozen food items intended for export.
The eligible financing areas include procurement of raw materials, establishment, expansion and modernization of processing plants, purchase of necessary machinery and equipment, construction of cold storage facilities, reopening of closed or partially operational processing plants, and installation of solar power projects to support production and preservation activities.

item.title: Two shot in Khulna amid joint forces' operations
item.description:
Two people, including a shrimp farm owner, were injured in a shooting by unidentified assailants in Khulna on Tuesday night, amid joint forces' operations to curb terrorism.
The incident took place around 9:30pm in the Burir Bhita area under Aranghata Police Station in the metropolitan city.
The injured shrimp farm owner was identified as Solaiman Fakir, also known as Solai, aged over 60.
The assailants opened fire on him, hitting him in the legs, hands and neck. As they fled, they fired another shot, injuring a van driver named Khalek.
Officer-in-Charge (Investigation) of Aranghata Police Station Md Monirul Islam said both victims were rescued by local residents and taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital.
He said the assailants targeted the shrimp farm owner around 9:30pm.
Monirul added that joint forces were conducting security operations in the area, as in other parts of the city, and police had stepped up raids to arrest criminals.
"Efforts are underway to identify and apprehend those involved in the shooting," he said.

item.title: Wife claims physically disabled man framed in Jessore court blast case
item.description:
A man accused in a case filed over a cocktail explosion on the Jessore court premises is physically unfit and unable to walk properly, his wife has claimed, alleging that he was implicated in the case to harass him despite having no involvement in political activities.
Rani Begum made the allegations at a press conference at Press Club Jessore around noon on Tuesday, where she read out a written statement on behalf of her husband, Jahidul Islam Tanvir.
She called for an impartial investigation into the incident, consideration of her husband's physical condition and medical needs, and security for their family.
According to the written statement, Tanvir runs a small fish business beside the Chanchra-Bablatala road to support his family and has no affiliation with any political party.
Rani alleged that after August 5, 2025, members of a force detained and beat her husband in front of their home over an incident. He and his mother were later taken to a police station but were released as no specific evidence was found against him.
She said Tanvir fell into a ditch around 1:30am on October 14 while heading out for his fish business, tearing the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) in his left leg. Following medical advice, he has been unable to move around normally.
The family has also been unable to arrange the necessary treatment due to financial constraints, she added.
However, Tanvir was named among 21 accused in a case filed over the cocktail explosions on theJessore court premises on November 12.
Questioning how a person unable to stand properly could have been involved in the incident, Rani demanded an impartial investigation into the allegations against her husband.
She said Tanvir is the family's sole breadwinner and that they have two sons. His illness, mounting medical expenses and the case have plunged the family into uncertainty.
Those present at the press conference included Tanvir's mother, Jesmin Sultana; aunt, Rekha Begum; another relative, Oheda Begum; neighbour Lamia Sultana; and his seven-year-old son, Taiyan Rahman.
The family also urged the authorities to identify the actual perpetrators and ensure their safety.
Meanwhile, police sources said Tanvir was arrested in connection with a drug-related case filed at a police station in 2023.
